analyst_view.overall: Olympiacos are 6th in the Europa League with 10 points and unbeaten in five European games, and they warmed up with a 6-2 home win over Iraklis on Sunday, after which Imanol Alguacil said this attacking, chance-creating style is how he wants them to play. AC Milan are 28th with 3 points, but their Serie A form has turned (3-1 over Inter, 2-1 at Genoa, 5-1 over Frosinone on Sunday), and Ruben Amorim said they must win in Piraeus or qualifying becomes very complicated. Gonçalo Ramos went off early against Frosinone, but reports on 23 November say it was only fatigue and he is available. The numbers already take off Olympiacos' absentees (Chiquinho for about a week, Hezze, Puerta, El Kaabi, Yazici) and Milan's (Perera suspended, Gabbia, Saelemaekers, Loftus-Cheek, Chukwueze); Tomori and Terracciano are doubtful and Leon Bailey is being checked after cramp against Iraklis. No referee is named yet; my small leans are a little more goals and cards because Milan have to chase the game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals (1.0 Olympiacos, 1.1 Milan), already cut for Chiquinho and Hezze being out and nudged up for both sides' recent scoring. I lean a little higher, to about 2.3: Amorim has called this a must-win, Ramos is fit after only fatigue, and Olympiacos just scored six at home, so a cagey game seems less likely than the numbers assume.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.0 corners, 5.3 for Olympiacos, already adding for their busy wide play and taking off Milan's low recent count. Alguacil says his side attack down the flanks when the middle is closed, which is what the numbers see; Milan are without wide men Saelemaekers and Chukwueze, also already in their low count, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, already trimmed for both sides' calm recent records. I lean slightly higher, to about 4.3: Milan must win to stay in the play-off race, Olympiacos want a top-eight place, and a full Karaiskakis tends to make these nights tense. No referee is named yet, so nothing on that side is counted.

shots.text: The numbers expect 24.7 shots, 15.4 for Olympiacos and 9.4 for Milan, already adding for Olympiacos' busy attack and cutting Milan for their thin recent output. Milan's attack has picked up in Serie A, but that form is already part of the numbers, and Bailey's fitness is the only doubt in Olympiacos' front line, so I stay at about 25.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, with Milan's lower recent accuracy already taken off. Pulisic and Ramos are Milan's main threats and both should play, while Olympiacos lack El Kaabi but have Mouandilmadji and Armando González scoring; nothing new beyond what the numbers know, so I stay at about 8.
